newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy government faces 23rd confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy government faces 23rd confidence vote.

text.p: The Italian centre-left government on Tuesday called a parliamentary confidence vote for the 23rd time since it took office last May.
Public Works Minister Paolo Costa called the vote in the lower house of parliament on a decree law aimed at speeding up approval for starting or resuming key state construction programmes.

The move was to sweep away some 400 amendments tabled by the separatist Northern League, whose obstructive tactics also forced the government to call a confidence vote last week on a similar decree law regarding Albanian refugees in Italy.

The League, which last year proclaimed the symbolic independence of northern Italy, has taken to obstructing most government decrees with a barrage of amendments to be debated in a bid to snarl parliamentary activity.
League deputy Pierluigi Copercini had earlier called the decree "hogwash, a sewn-up, cobbled-together law" and challenged the government to call a confidence vote.
Under the terms of a confidence vote, blocking amendments are swept away and the house votes on a package with a simple yes or no vote.
The vote cannot be held until 24 hours have elapsed from it being formally called in parliament.
If the government loses, it falls.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government relies on the support of the hard-left Communist Refoundation in the lower house for a majority but is not seen in danger in the vote which is a technical measure to prevent a decree lapsing.
Under a constitutional court ruling, decree laws passed by the cabinet have a 60-day life and must be either passed by parliament within that time or lapse.

The construction decree law, to create special authorities to streamline the approval process for starting or resuming public works that have been long frozen or stalled, must be approved by the lower house by May 25.
The upper house has already approved the measure, of particular importance to impoverished southern Italy where unemployment is high.
Many construction projects throughout Italy have been frozen for years since a corruption scandal exposed by graft-busting magistrates swept away Italy's old political order in 1992.
Some such projects have been exposed as lucrative sources of kickbacks and bribes from contractors.
